subject: Clarify SOC 2 reporting boundaries & rollforward procedure
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@auditscape.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Wright <tom.wright@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — reporting boundary and rollforward clarification

Hi Priya,

We're reviewing the SOC 2 Type II materials you uploaded for the Mar 1–Mar 31, 2026 period for Acme Analytics. A couple of clarifications before we finalize procedures:

1) Calendar boundaries — are the report "day" boundaries recorded in UTC or in a specific regional timezone? For example: is an event at 00:00:00 UTC on 2026-03-31 considered inside Mar 31 or Mar 30 for your capture? Please state the canonical definition you used when assembling the period.

2) Rollforward / continuity evidence — for point-in-time evidence we often ask for a short rollforward that demonstrates continuity from 23:59:XX on the prior day into the beginning of the next day (requests in-flight, cache flushes, any asynchronous commits). Do you maintain an established rollforward process or a runbook we can reference?

3) Exceptions — if there are known short windows where events are asynchronously persisted (e.g., 30s commit window), please disclose and provide how those are flagged in logs.

If you can provide a brief written description and 1–2 log extracts (CSV with request_id, timestamp, event_type) that tie to the March 31 boundary, that will be sufficient for the auditor's sampling. Would also welcome a short 20–30 minute call to walk through.

Thanks —
Elena
Elena Soto
Senior Audit Manager, Auditscape
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@auditscape.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Wright <tom.wright@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — reporting boundary and rollforward clarification

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and I'm attaching a short overview + one sample extract for Mar 31.

1) Canonical boundary: all SOC 2 reporting dates for Redwood are normalized to UTC for evidence collection and reporting purposes. A "report day" runs 00:00:00.000 UTC through 23:59:59.999 UTC. We note UTC on report pages and in the cover memo.

2) Rollforward/runbook: we maintain a documented rollforward procedure that captures the last-second in-flight requests and the immediate replay of any asynchronous persistence operations. The normal operational window is a 30-second buffer after 00:00:00 UTC during which we capture final commit events and tag them as part of the prior-day rollover. The attached "redwood-soc2-rollforward-overview.pdf" describes the steps; the CSV sample is a small extract showing request_id, timestamp (UTC), and event_type for a handful of transactions around 2026-03-31T23:59:58+00:00.

3) Exceptions: there are two known scenarios we flag: (a) long-running background batch jobs that persist after the 30s buffer (these are flagged as "deferred_commit" and require corroboration via job run ids), and (b) manual admin replays for failed writes (flagged as "admin_replay"). Both are documented and surfaced to the SOC evidence bucket; examples are included in the CSV.

We can provide a signed bridge letter that lists operating exceptions for the period and a mapping file that ties sampled request_ids back to primary logs. I'm happy to schedule a 25-minute walkthrough — I'm available Mon/Tue afternoons PST.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-rollforward-overview.pdf; evidence-log-extract-20260331.csv

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Compliance (Embedded)
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@auditscape.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Wright <tom.wright@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — reporting boundary and rollforward clarification

Priya —

Thanks, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups after reviewing the PDF/CSV:

- Can you confirm the exact implementation detail for in-flight requests at midnight across regions? Acme runs clients in us-west and eu-west; we want to ensure cross-region request timestamps are all normalized before sampling. Do you correlate using server-side UTC timestamps or client-supplied times?

- For the 30s buffer: is the buffer configurable per workload or global? If configurable, please indicate which workloads used longer windows during March and why.

- Please provide the requested bridge letter (signed) describing any planned or ad-hoc operational exceptions that could affect point-in-time evidence. We will attach that to our Type II working papers.

- Finally, for sampling, can you provide a short mapping file with three example request_ids plus the log shard/filename where they appear? That will let us validate the chain.

If you can upload the bridge letter and the mapping CSV before our call, we'll use that time to walk through the implementation.

Elena
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@auditscape.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Wright <tom.wright@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — reporting boundary and rollforward clarification

Elena —

Adding a few operational specifics to help your sampling and to prepare the bridge letter.

- Timestamp canonicalization: all server-side events are stamped in UTC at ingest (monotonic server clock). Client-supplied times are stored in metadata but we never rely on them for audit rollups. Cross-region requests are correlated via a global request_id assigned at the edge load balancer.

- Buffer behaviour: the 30s rollforward buffer is a global policy for user-facing request commits. Two backend maintenance workloads (index_compaction and analytics-backfill) may have extended persistence windows; during March we had one scheduled analytics-backfill on 2026-03-18 that extended into 2026-03-19 00:00:42 UTC — that job is flagged as "deferred_commit" and excluded from the primary point-in-time sample unless specifically requested. We'll list those exceptions in the bridge letter.

- Mapping sample: attached is request-id-mapping-202603.csv with three example request_ids and the exact log shard path where they appear (s3://redwood-evidence/2026/03/31/shard-07.log). Those three map to the rows you saw in the evidence CSV.

- Bridge letter: we'll produce a one-page signed bridge letter that enumerates the standard 30s buffer, the two exception categories, and calls out the analytics-backfill on 2026-03-18 as an example. Draft is attached (bridge-letter-template.docx) — we will sign and return the PDF once you confirm the wording.

If useful, we can run the 25-minute call Tue 11:00 AM PST (Tue 18:00 UTC) to walk through the CSV/TIMELINE.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: bridge-letter-template.docx; request-id-mapping-202603.csv
